audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows read 'Skill' and two read 'Vayne' where the packet chart and the already-audited Sett side both give Vayne only Level 1 and the two-item row.
audit.why: Sett has no ability at level 1 that reaches Vayne, so the first wave is hers; from 2 through first item, Facebreaker (16s rank 1) into Haymaker out-trades her, and The Show Stopper at 6 removes her spacing entirely.
audit.corrected: Vayne, Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Vayne — proposed as matched full/content pairs with the ratings that go with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5] called the first item Vayne's spike; the mirror and the packet both give that row to Sett, and level 6 was written as if Final Hour mattered there.
audit.why: The Show Stopper is 120/100/80s and is a displacement — Final Hour grants attack damage, Tumble invisibility and a shorter Tumble, none of which refuse a grab. Vayne's genuine spike is two items of Silver Bolts, whose true damage does not care what Sett stacks.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and first item are his; two items are yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing stated what Haymaker actually punishes, and spikes[3] claimed Condemn 'interrupts his W wind-up and R engage' without support.
audit.why: Haymaker stores the damage Sett takes as Grit and spends it for a shield plus true damage in the centre of the punch — so a long trade into him funds it. Condemn is a knockback that moves him out of the centre band; whether it cancels the cast is not in the kit data, so it is not asserted.
audit.corrected: Chip trades feed Haymaker's Grit; Condemn displaces him out of the true-damage centre.
sources: kit: Haymaker text and shield/trueDamage flags

edits.before: Kite with autos and never let him touch you. Identify how Sett contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Sett has one ability at 1 and no way to close: your range wins the first wave outright. Poke him off the melee minions.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Facebreaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: E-into-W is the whole trade: Facebreaker stuns on 16s at rank 1, then Haymaker cashes the Grit you fed it as true damage.

edits.before: Final Hour stealth-tumbles break every engage pattern onto you. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sett's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: The Show Stopper carries you off for 120s at rank 1, and Final Hour's stealth does nothing to a displacement. Do not fight at 6.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Facebreaker's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is online, but Haymaker still out-damages it. Fight only when Facebreaker's 16s is down.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Haymaker stores the damage you deal him and returns it as true.

edits.before: Yours: two items of Silver Bolts true damage shred his stacked health, and Condemn (E) interrupts his W wind-up and R engage. Kite his cooldowns and he can't land a fist on you.
edits.after: Yours: two items of Silver Bolts true damage shred his stacked health, and Condemn knocks him out of Haymaker's centre band before the true damage lands. Kite his 16s E and he never reaches you.

notes: Chart rows proposed as matched pairs in one group, with the two ratings that contradicted the new sides. Whether Condemn's knockback cancels a Haymaker cast, and whether The Show Stopper's grab can be cleansed or Flash-buffered, are not in the kit data and were not asserted anywhere.
